charts.title: protocell-autopoietic-movie
charts.caption: Animated GIF of the autopoietic closed-loop run: a Gaussian-annulus membrane ring on a 64x64 field, its production loop gated on the boundary staying topologically closed and self-limited by enclosed area, HOLDS its ring -- the enclosed interior plateaus into a homeostatic steady state rather than dissolving or filling solid. The membrane persists because the process inside the boundary maintains the organization that keeps that process possible (the paper's §Self-organized processes criterion). Re-baked over the same run cited in this study's behavior tests, for provenance.

charts.title: protocell-vesicle-control-movie
charts.caption: Animated GIF of the negative-control run: the IDENTICAL seed and wiring with production knocked out (k_prod=0). With no internal maintenance loop the membrane is a mere vesicle -- the ring decays and diffuses, its topological closure is lost, and the enclosed interior falls to zero. Watch it side by side with the autopoietic GIF: the single differing variable (k_prod) is the difference between persistence and dissipation. Re-baked over the same run cited in this study's behavior tests.

charts.title: autopoiesis-metrics
charts.caption: Interactive Plotly panel of the closed-loop run, synced to the GIF's time axis: the enclosed interior area (the closure/boundary-integrity metric, plateauing at a homeostatic ~149 px) plotted with the membrane mass (the mass-held gate). The two traces together are the load-bearing evidence that persistence is genuine self-maintenance -- a bounded interior held against decay, not a filled solid blob and not a near-zero-mass ghost ring. Interactive: hover for exact per-tick values.
